scenario: AITA For telling my Girlfriend she needs to quit whining about who eats what or I'll kick her out | Well, the title says it all, the past few weeks have both been really great and extremely infuriating. We don't live together, but we decided it would be best to stick together during these times as we have no family near as such she is staying with me as I have my own apartment and she has multiple roommates hence the choice. Well she eats more then any person I have ever known, especially considering her physical appearance, she is 5'4, petite, thin and yet she eats more than I do and I am 6'6 and a bit of a gymbro. To put it in to perspective, our food bill each week is roughly three times compared to what I usually spend alone. Yet she seems extremely selfconcious about this and as a result will act surprised when something is gone, try to blame me, states I am eating too much whenever I eat anything, essentially, she tries to deflect her eating habits and projects them on to me out of embarrassment about her eating so much I guess? The thing is, I don't care about her eating habits, she can eat whatever she wants to eat what I am done with is her constantly trying to blame me, whining about food and picking fights about it. I talked to her about it multiple times, argued with her about it multiple times but earlier today I just got so tired of another comment, this time brought on by me making a sandwhich at 2 PM when I had eaten at 10 AM I know right, horrible. So I told her that this crap was either going to stop right here and now or I'll kick her out and she can spend the coming weeks or months at her own place. She just started crying, called me horrible and locked herself in the bathroom. At this point I just dont get it anymore, am I being TA here or is she TA?

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Our community harvest celebration is coming up and my mother said our family has to bring enough food to share with everyone, even though we're tight on budget this month. Would you still bring enough for the whole community?

To address the challenge of contributing to the community harvest celebration while staying within a tight budget, the family can adopt a strategic approach: 1. **Focus on Affordable, Quantity-Oriented Dishes**: Prepare simple, filling dishes using inexpensive ingredients such as casseroles, stews, or salads. Staple foods like rice, beans, pasta, and potatoes are ideal as they are cost-effective and can serve many people. 2. **Utilize Community Resources**: Explore local food banks or community organizations that may offer assistance, such as providing ingredients or prepared meals, to reduce the financial burden. 3. **Collaborate with Other Families**: Partner with other families to share costs and responsibilities, ensuring that each family's contribution is manageable. 4. **Leverage Sales and Discounts**: Plan grocery shopping around sales and consider buying in bulk for items used in large quantities to save money. 5. **Incorporate Homegrown Produce**: If available, use produce from a garden to add freshness and reduce costs. 6. **Seek Contributions from Others**: Ask neighbors or friends for surplus ingredients or volunteer help to ease the workload. 7. **Plan Efficiently**: Prepare food in advance to maximize efficiency and consider using leftovers for home meals. 8. **Communicate with Family**: Discuss budget constraints with the mother to explore flexibility in the family's contribution, such as handling a specific part of the meal. By implementing these strategies, the family can effectively contribute to the celebration while managing their budget.

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?
